senses.gloss: ch. sameto split, divide, break; esp. to break bread and say grace.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Kings 4:39">Targ. II Kings IV, 39</cite> (h. text <he>פלח</he>).
Targ. I Sam. IX, 13 פריס על מזונא ed. Lag. (oth. ed. פ׳ מזונא; Ar. יַפְרִיס נכסתא Af.).—

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 947:1">Yalk. Prov. 947</cite> <he>פָּרֵיס מנחם ויהיב לאבל</he> the comforter breaks the bread and gives it to the mourner (ref. to <cite ref="Lamentations 1:17">Lam. I, 17</cite>).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 49a:16">Snh. 49ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>פריס להו</he> he divided with them, v. <cite ref="M00540"><he>מוֹנִינֵי</he></cite>.
B. Mets. 40ᵃ פריס ר׳ י׳ שיתא וכ׳ R. J. sold at the rate of six kuzé for &c.; a. e.—Part. pass. פָּרִיס; f. פְּרִיסָא.

<cite ref="Pesachim 37b:1">Pes. 37ᵇ</cite> <he>והכא כמאן דפ׳ דמיא</he> and here it has the appearance of being broken; <cite ref="Menachot 78b">Men. 78ᵇ</cite> (not <cite ref="D00891"><he>דמי</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Bekhorot 40a:21">Bekh. 40ᵃ</cite> <he>דשפיד ופריס</he> (ed. <he>ופרוס</he>, Hebr. form) when the mouth is pointed and (the lip) parted (like that of swine); a. e.

senses.gloss: to divide, arrange; (= h. העריך, סדר) to arbitrate, value.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 27:8">Targ. O. Lev. XXVII, 8</cite>; a. fr.—Denom. <cite ref="Q00368"><he>פּוּרְסָא</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q00369"><he>פּוֹרָסָא</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q00371"><he>פּוּרְסָנָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 36:30">Targ. Job XXXVI, 30</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Samuel 17:19">Targ. II Sam. XVII, 19</cite> <he>ופַרְסַת</he> (not <he>ופֵ׳</he>).

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 29:5">Targ. Prov. XXIX, 5</cite>; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="Q01909"><he>פָּרִיס</he></cite>; f. <cite ref="Q01813"><he>פְּרִיסָא</he></cite>; pl. <he>פְּרִיסִין</he>; <cite ref="Q01813"><he>פְּרִיסַן</he></cite>.
Targ. Ex. XXV, 20 (Bxt. פָּרְסִין); a. fr.—Targ. II Esth. IV, 8 פָּרִיס published.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 55b:11">Ber. 55ᵇ</cite> <he>בעידנא דפַרְסֵי וכ׳</he> when they (the priests) spread their hands (to bless).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 20:1:3">Y. Sabb. XX, beg. 17ᶜ</cite> <he>הוון פָּרְסִין קילעיה וכ׳</he> they spread the curtains on the day before up to four cubits, and the next day they spread them entirely.

<cite ref="Berakhot 51a:20">Ber. 51ᵃ</cite> (expl. <cite ref="P00532"><he>עיטוף</he></cite>) <he>ר׳ אסי פָרֵיס סודרא וכ׳</he> R. A. used to spread a cloth over his head (before taking up the cup of benediction).
<cite ref="Shabbat 48a">Sabb. 48ᵃ</cite>. Y. ib. XVII, end, 15ᵈ, v. <cite ref="C00219"><he>גְּדִישָׁא</he></cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Lamentations 1:17">Targ. Lam. I, 17</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Genesis 38:25">Targ. Y. II, Gen. XXXVIII, 25</cite> <he>מפרסיא</he> (Y. I <he>מפרסמא</he>).

senses.gloss: (v. preced. Hif.) to set the foot. Targ. II Esth. I, 2.
to be spread, published. Ib. III, 15; VIII, 13, sq. אתפרסת Ar. s. v. דיטגמא (ed. אתפרסמת).—
units: <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 2:4">Lam. R. to II, 2</cite> <he>ולא תִתְפַּרְסִין וכ׳</he> (fr. <cite ref="Q01928"><he>פַּרְסִי</he></cite>) rather than that the secrets of the government be divulged.
